544921|2026-06.headline: Arcil Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 107% to INR143 crores on INR1,066 crores recoveries (up 151%), with acquisitions seasonally light at INR353 crores.
544921|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a recovery-led quarter: total recoveries rose 151% to INR1,066 crores and standalone PAT more than doubled to INR143 crores, driven by a large corporate resolution. Acquisitions were INR353 crores (Arcil share INR143 crores), about INR150 crores lower than Q1 FY26, consistent with the seasonal pattern where most acquisitions occur in Q4. AUM was INR19,574 crores (up 16% YoY) and borrowings fell sequentially to INR1,100 crores, with management expecting to draw down more in the coming quarters. Consolidated PAT was INR59 crores versus standalone INR143 crores, and management urged investors to assess the company on a standalone and full-year basis.

financial_highlights.change: +151% vs INR425 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Write-back of security receipts, fees and expenses written off earlier

financial_highlights.change: +107% YoY; PAT margin about 52% of total income
From INR1,200 crores in March 2026; debt-equity 0.34x

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: About 68% of AUM and a corporate book of about INR13,000 crores; recoveries are chunky and event-driven, which drove the Q1 spike.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: About 24% of AUM; over 3.29 million retail borrowers on the platform, with steady granular repayments. Retail and SME rose from about 21% to 31% of AUM since March 2024.

segments.name: SME
segments.commentary: About 8% of AUM; management treats SME as an independent business it wants to grow.

segments.name: Collection as a service
segments.commentary: Still at infrastructure-build and proof-of-concept stage with own assets and a few NBFCs; no revenue or pipeline numbers given.

guidance_outlook: No numerical AUM or acquisition guidance; management expects AUM to rise while acquisitions are matched by equal resolutions, with resolutions of about 20-25% of opening AUM each year.
Management expects acquisitions to rise through Q2 and Q3, with pipelines described as strong, and to draw down more borrowings and marginally increase leverage.
Write-backs of previously written-off assets are expected to decline over time; maximum write-offs over the next three years are cumulatively under INR100 crores.
Management expects its fee income momentum to be maintained, though it said the Q1 write-back was not a full-year trend.
capex_capacity: Borrowings were reduced to INR1,100 crores in Q1 to fund acquisitions later in the year; cash and bank balances INR252 crores, which management says gives ample capacity to fund acquisitions.

Own investment in AUM was about INR4,200 crores (about 22% of AUM) as of June; the FY26 average investment ratio was about 33% (INR2,000 crores on INR6,000 crores acquired), and Q1 FY27 is running at about 40%.
Mandatory minimum SR investment is 15%; co-investor deals allow as low as 2.5%.
Last-mile funding of up to 25% of acquired loan value is available to support turnarounds.
demand_pricing: Industry stress (banks and NBFCs, including SMA, NPA and written-off) is about INR23 lakh crores per management, growing about INR1 lakh crore a year; ARCs participate in roughly 10%.
Special mention accounts were about 30% of new ARC acquisitions in FY25, up from about 14% in FY24 (CRISIL data cited by management).
Acquisition cost held at 26-27% of dues every year; Arcil's AUM is about 14% of the INR1.4 lakh crore dues under management.
Arcil's share of industry AUM rose from 11% to 15% over two years; share of new acquisitions was 17% in FY26 on about INR6,000 crores acquired.
Management attributed improved industry recovery rates (cited as moving from about 35% to about 85%) to a stronger economy and real estate recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Why has industry recovery rate risen from about 35% to about 85%, and will it improve further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an improving economy lets ARCs buy cheaply in stress and resolve at higher rates later; real estate assets stressed four to five years ago are now repaying and redeeming SRs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings fall sequentially, and will they be drawn again?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowings are seasonal: lines are drawn mainly at year-end for acquisitions. With a strong pipeline for Q2 and Q3, management expects to draw down more and marginally increase leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Is there AUM guidance for FY27, and why is the retail mix rising?
qa_highlights.answer: No AUM target was given; AUM is expected to rise with acquisitions balanced by equal resolutions, roughly 20-25% of opening AUM resolved each year. Mix reflects asset availability, with no target balance.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the INR120 crore write-back of earlier written-off assets, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Write-backs are event-based recoveries from legal cases. Management cited about INR288 crores in FY24, INR100 crores in FY25 and INR66 crores in FY26, said Q1 should not be a full-year trend, and said maximum write-offs over the next three years total under INR100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is fee income, given fee income is about 2.4% of AUM annualised versus 1.4% a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management fee nearly doubled YoY and is about 45-50% of total fees. Fee income also depends on collections and resolution, not AUM alone. Management said the momentum should be maintained, and fees are earned only on recoveries, with the legacy book carrying no fee.

qa_highlights.question: What are the IRR and vintage profile of the book, and how is the 15% minimum SR investment used?
qa_highlights.answer: General IRR targeted in the high-20s to 20-22% range. Over-8-year vintage AUM is 34%, fully written off on a regulatory basis. Mandatory SR investment is 15%, as low as 2.5% in co-investor deals; own share is 22% of AUM, and Q1 FY27 investment is running at about 40% of acquisitions versus 33% in FY26.

risks_watch: Quarterly volatility: Q1 recoveries and PAT were lumpy corporate resolutions; management said Q1 should not be read as a trend.
Write-back income (INR120 crores in Q1, INR66 crores in FY26) is event-based and expected to decline as write-offs have stopped; monitor the share of PAT it contributes.
Acquisitions in Q1 were INR353 crores, down about INR150 crores YoY; the Q2 and Q3 ramp and the pipeline conversion are not quantified.
Leverage rising from 0.34x debt-equity as borrowings are drawn for acquisitions; watch the debt-equity ratio and CRAR (72.5%) as own-investment share rises towards 40%.
Consolidated PAT of INR59 crores versus standalone INR143 crores; investors may focus on standalone, which management said is the basis for regulatory ratios.
Collection-as-a-service remains at proof-of-concept stage with no revenue, client count or targets disclosed.
Management did not comment on the effect of rising repo rates and retail stress on consumer behaviour.
key_quotes: Q1 was a recovery -led quarter. Recovery rose 150%, and profit after tax more than doubled, driven by strong corporate resolution, while acquisition followed our usual seasonal pattern.
So while we can tell you that our general IRR across the businesses historically is on the higher 20s, you know, and, you know, 20%,-22%, kind of thing.
We are not giving any guidance on these numbers. Yes.

So as we have collected INR120 crores this quarter, which of course is, should not be taken as a trend for the full year, but if you look at our past financials, we continue to get very large sum in as a collection against the written-off assets.
544921|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the recovery-led Q1 and the long-term outlook, but cautious on forward numbers: management gave no AUM, acquisition or CaaS guidance, citing the lack of visibility and the need to judge the company over full years and on a standalone basis. Responses on the write-back line and the borrowing plan were direct, while the answer on consumer stress was deferred as too early to comment.

544921|2026-09.headline: ARCIL H1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 54% to INR290 crores on 48% higher total income of INR516 crores; acquisitions up 18% to INR1,707 crores.
544921|2026-09.overview: ARCIL reported H1 FY27 (six months to September 30, 2026) with AUM up 21% to INR20,274 crores and total income up 48% to INR516 crores. Q2 acquisitions reached INR1,354 crores, up 43% year on year, after a weak Q1 of INR353 crores, consistent with the seasonal pattern management described. Q2 recoveries of INR1,069 crores were below the strong prior-year Q2 that included large corporate resolutions, and an ECL provision taken in Q1 was partly reversed in Q2. Management asked investors to judge the company on standalone results and over longer periods, and gave no numerical guidance.

vs INR1,339 crores in Q2 FY26
+54% vs INR189 crores in H1 FY26
vs INR37 crores; management cited INR140 crores for H1 in the Q&A

segments.name: AUM mix
segments.commentary: Corporate about 66%, retail about 25% and SME about 9% of AUM, versus about 69%, 24% and 8% a year earlier. Retail AUM crossed INR5,000 crores for the first time.

segments.name: Corporate acquisitions
segments.commentary: About INR700 crores of the H1 acquisitions were corporate; the remaining about INR1,000 crores were SME and retail. Corporate AUM is about INR13,000 crores.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: Fee and other income rose 82% to INR227 crores in H1, and management said quarterly fee income has stabilised at about INR115-120 crores.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance on AUM, acquisitions or H2 profitability; management pointed to historical performance and regularity of recoveries.
Management said H2 is seasonally the stronger acquisition period, with about 60% of last year's acquisitions in H2, and described the pipeline as healthy.
Write-backs are expected to be lower in H2 than in H1, but will remain a recurring part of revenue.
Investment upsides have run at INR200 crores-plus a year for the last 2-3 years, and management expects a consistent flow.
Management said fee plus investment upside should be about 70-80% of total revenue over time, with management fee run-rate of about INR450 crores per annum.
Collection-as-a-service pilots with a couple of lenders are expected to scale in H2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Borrowings rose to INR1,224 crores to fund Q2 acquisitions; management said the balance sheet can fund H2.
ARCIL invested INR718 crores of its own capital in H1 acquisitions, an investment ratio of 42% (33% last year).
Operating footprint is 15 offices across 12 states, with technology and analytics investment ongoing.
Priorities include growing mid-sized corporate assets, raising retail and SME share, scaling collection as a service, and selectively evaluating stressed microfinance portfolios.
demand_pricing: Management estimates total stress at about INR23.7 lakh crores (CRISIL, FY26), of which about INR15.9 lakh crores is NPAs and written-off loans; ARCs buy below 10% of the pool annually per management's internal estimate.
Unsecured retail assets were acquired at single-digit percent of dues and secured retail at mid-40s percent, per management.
Management said about 70% of the last two years' acquisitions were on an AUM basis, and that the majority of H1 acquisitions were structured SR deals rather than cash deals.
Management said ARCs do not currently participate in agri or gold loan stress; microfinance is being evaluated selectively.
Management said competition from NARCL is focused on very large assets, and ARCIL differentiates by covering all asset classes.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors model lumpy non-fee revenue such as upsides and writebacks across the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said large corporate recoveries are lumpy but recur because of the large corporate book, so regularity should be judged rather than single items. Writebacks were INR125 crores in Q1 and lower in Q2, totalling INR140 crores for H1, and are expected to be lower in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ECL impairment reverse in Q2, and what is the sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the ECL provision is quarter-to-quarter, rising when receivables increase, as in Q1, and partly reversed in Q2. Annual ECL provisioning under RBI rules is about INR15-20 crores, which he called unsubstantial.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income grow 82% against 21% AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income comes from acquisitions and also includes collection-based fees, so it depends on both AUM and collections. Quarterly fee income has stabilised at about INR115-120 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Are there signs of stress and competitive intensity affecting the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the existing stress pool of over INR23 lakh crores is large enough for growth, and that ARCIL is positioned with 0.37x debt-to-equity and 70.5% CAR to buy any new stress. Competition is rising in retail, where ARCIL is investing in technology and its CAS platform.

qa_highlights.question: How do retail and SME acquisitions carry write-off risk, and what mix is being bought?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retail presence dates to 2008 and that the 3-4 year resolution cycle, plus in-house collections, limits write-off risk. H1 acquisitions were about INR700 crores corporate and about INR1,000 crores SME and retail. Write-offs occur about eight years after acquisition, and management expects only a very small amount to cross that threshold over the next three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why invest more in structured SR deals if they carry no upside income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said structured deals return the IRR mostly as regular fee income, while cash deals give larger upsides later in the holding period. Average investment across H1 acquisitions was 42%.

risks_watch: Lumpiness of corporate recoveries and writebacks: H1 writebacks of INR129-140 crores are expected to fall in H2, which could weigh on other income.
Acquisition seasonality: H2 needs to deliver for full-year acquisition growth; management gave no numerical guidance.
Rising ECL provisions when receivables grow, as seen in Q1 FY27, and reversal in Q2.
Higher finance costs (INR43 crores vs INR7.5 crores) as borrowings fund acquisitions, with debt rising to INR1,224 crores.
Entry into microfinance and expected growth in competition in retail and SME; the company said it is still testing the microfinance market.
Industry AUM has been flat per the Q&A; management attributed this to recoveries and write-offs by some ARCs rather than a structural issue.
544921|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the long-term runway and balance sheet, but deliberately cautious on near-term numbers: management repeatedly declined to guide on acquisitions, H2 profitability or AUM, and asked investors to look at standalone results over longer periods. The Q2 recovery and ECL items were explained as timing effects rather than trend changes.
key_quotes: Buy with discipline, resolve with urgency and deploy capital with a clear focus on returns.
We are not giving any guidance on any specific numbers.
As we explained earlier, write-backs continues to be part and parcel of our main revenue stream.
So we do not see any risk of write-offs going forward in retail, SME, and even in corporate book.

rows.why: Quarterly fee income has stabilised at about INR115-120 crores, against a management fee run-rate of about INR450 crores a year, supporting recurring revenue.

rows.label: Borrowings rising to fund acquisitions
rows.why: Borrowings rose to INR1,224 crores (from INR1,100 crores at June 30) with debt-to-equity 0.37x, and finance costs rose to INR43 crores from INR7.5 crores, though management says the balance sheet can fund H2.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term runway, balance sheet (CAR 70.5%, D/E 0.37x) and the H2 pipeline, but cautious on near-term numbers and declined to give guidance, while analysts pressed on lumpy writebacks, the Q2 ECL reversal and fee growth versus AUM growth.

544923|2026-09.headline: Veegaland Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28.7% YoY to INR106.34 crore and PAT rose 92% to INR15.99 crore, with PAT margin at 14.7%.
544923|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR106.34 crore, up 28.66% YoY, with EBITDA (incl. other income) of INR22.78 crore (up 77%) and EBITDA margin of 20.90%, up 550 bps. PAT was INR15.99 crore, up 92%, at a 14.70% margin. H1 FY27 revenue was INR180.66 crore (up 45%) and PAT was INR25.71 crore (up 123%). Management attributed margin gains to luxe-series mix, cost efficiencies on near-complete projects, and treasury income on RERA-linked fixed deposits. The company listed on 18 September 2026 after a INR210 crore IPO.

segments.name: Premium / mid-premium
segments.commentary: Higher-volume, lower-ticket segment; management says demand is strong across segments. Average selling price rose from INR8,539 per sq ft in June to INR9,286 in September, per the call.

segments.name: Luxe series
segments.commentary: High-margin, low-volume; two luxe projects, with Fortune launched and already in ongoing status. Luxe launches in H2 FY26 are now flowing through revenue and lifting margins.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give pre-sales or GDV projections; it expects strong momentum but declined to quantify it.
Three upcoming projects with estimated GDV of about INR450 crore (Sarovar, East Port, and Fortune, which has since launched) are slated for launch in Q3 FY27 or early Q4 FY27.
Land-bank launches expected 6 to 9 months out; management declined to give GDV for them.
Margins expected to hold steady on an unchanged product mix, though material prices are being monitored.
Leverage is not to exceed about 0.5:1 in the mid-term; no significant increase in debt is planned.
Proceeds of the IPO are earmarked for ongoing projects, planned acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
capex_capacity: Land bank is about 6.4 acres, mostly in Kochi with some in Kozhikode; the company holds no Trivandrum land after launching Lluvia Gardens (163 units).
Portfolio is 12 ongoing and 3 upcoming projects: 2 in Thrissur, 2 in Kozhikode, 3 in Trivandrum and the rest in Kochi.
Projects are boutique apartment schemes of about 75 to 150 units; preferred land parcels are around 1 to 1.25 acres for faster turnaround.
Management is scouting new land to support a FY29 plan and is considering new geographies in neighbouring areas; no specific location announced.
Unencumbered cash is about INR180 crore, with further funds in RERA escrow accounts.
demand_pricing: Pre-sales value rose 37.6% YoY and area booked rose 19.6% YoY; gross collections rose 88.2% YoY.
Q2 pre-sales were about INR174 crore.
Amora (Kochi) was 68% booked within about 4 months of launch.
NRI buyers account for about 48% to 50% of sales, and Middle East-based Malayalis are buying a second home in Kerala.
Q1 FY27 pre-sales were unusually high, which management attributes to Middle East conflict-driven demand.
Cancellations after agreement execution are very low; management says cancelled units were resold at higher prices.
Management says its prices are below listed national peers such as Sobha and Prestige for comparable offerings.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans for projects outside Kerala?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating neighbouring geographies but has named none yet; it will announce once plans are finalised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook, and can margins return to the FY23 level of about 21-23%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable on a stable product mix, citing luxe-series mix and cost efficiencies; it gave no project-level margins or FY23 comparison.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR1,080 crore order book is still unrecognised, and over what period?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR500 crore is unrecognised and should be recognised up to FY30-31, not linearly, with larger chunks in FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is incremental borrowing needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said balance-sheet borrowing is not needed but project term loans will be taken; leverage will stay below about 0.5:1 in the mid-term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current cancellation rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no figure; it said post-agreement cancellations are very few because buyers are almost all end-users.

qa_highlights.question: How will sales hold up given rate hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said premium and luxe buyers are less rate-sensitive and that NRI buyers often pay without bank loans; it cited a 25 bps hike.

Material cost inputs (steel, cables, PVC, sanitary) are being watched; management says there is no margin squeeze yet.

544925|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to ₹78.5 crore and EBITDA rose 52% to ₹15.1 crore, with margin at 19.2%.
544925|2026-09.overview: Maharaja & Speedex reported H1 FY27 (first earnings call after listing): revenue from operations of ₹78.5 crore (up 36% YoY), EBITDA of ₹15.1 crore (up 52%, margin 19.2% vs 17.2%) and PAT of ₹9.9 crore (up 50%). Gross margin expanded about 447 bps sequentially, helped by lower outsourcing, a richer mix of value-added products and an ~8% price increase. Capacity stands at 72 lakh bottles per year after internal-accrual additions, with a 31 lakh unit IPO-funded expansion due in Q4 FY27 taking it to ~103 lakh. Short-term borrowings of ~₹22.7 crore were fully repaid and D/E is 0.04.

financial_highlights.change: +36% YoY; +21% over H2 FY26 as stated
management attributed to lower outsourcing, mix and price increase

financial_highlights.metric: Employee cost as % of sales (6 months)

segments.name: OEM/ODM (B2B)

544937|2026-09.headline: NSE Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 23% YoY to ₹2,578 crore on revenue from operations up 11% to ₹4,067 crore.

Q2 FY26 expenses included a ₹1,297 crore SEBI settlement provision, so reported expenditure fell 51% YoY; excluding it, expenditure rose 10%. 544940|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 standalone total income rose about 182% to INR52.37 crore, with PAT up about 395% to INR6.85 crore, as a carried-over order book was executed.

Working capital remained high at about INR73 crore, which management tied to government payment cycles, with collections expected in H2 and December-January.

544949|2026-09.headline: Swastika Infra H1 FY27 revenue INR207 crores (+5% YoY), Q2 revenue +42% to INR188 crores; unexecuted order book about INR1,420 crores.

544962|2026-09.headline: AceVector H1 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR285.5 crore, while Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss widened to INR8.6 crore from INR2.2 crore.
544962|2026-09.overview: AceVector reported H1 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations of INR285.5 crore, up 17% YoY, and Q2 FY27 revenue of INR151.2 crore, up 17% from INR129.3 crore. Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss was INR8.6 crore versus a INR2.2 crore loss in Q2 FY26, but it narrowed more than 50% from about INR18.3 crore in Q1 despite festive marketing spend. Snapdeal's overall NMV growth slowed to 10% in H1 as festive timing shifted from Q2 to Q3, while fashion NMV grew 31%. Unicommerce revenue grew 15% to INR110.4 crore, with management guiding to a return to higher profitability in H2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR2.2 crore in Q2 FY26; narrowed from loss of about INR18.3 crore in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: Growth 31% YoY; fashion share of business about 68%+
financial_highlights.change: fashion share up from 57% in H1 FY26
delivered units up 16%; app-delivered units up 23%

segments.name: Snapdeal (value fashion marketplace)
segments.commentary: Fashion NMV up 31% YoY in H1 and fashion now about 68%+ of business; overall NMV up 10% and delivered units up 16%, with October first 15 days units up 60% YoY. Contribution margin about 10% of NMV on ~INR400 ASP, giving ~INR40 unit contribution; zero commission to sellers, asset-light and zero-inventory.

segments.name: Unicommerce (SaaS enablement)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR110.4 crore, up 15% YoY, with usage-linked per-transaction pricing. Management has stepped up investment over three quarters, which moderated adjusted EBITDA; guides 15%+ growth in Uniware and 20%+ growth in Shipway from Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Unicommerce expects 15%+ growth in Uniware and 20%+ growth in Shipway from Q4 FY27 onwards.
Pace of incremental investment at Unicommerce expected to moderate in H2 FY27, with higher profitability and stronger operating leverage targeted in H2 FY27.
Snapdeal expects its overall business to continue growing in the 30s (%) going forward, per Achint Setia, and the fashion/home/beauty category mix to stay broadly similar.
Full picture on Q2 plus Q3 festive impact to come with Q3 results; no quantified festive impact given.
capex_capacity: Management described the model as asset-light with very low infrastructure requirement; no capex or capacity figures were given.
Snapdeal is zero-inventory and runs on third-party logistics; Unicommerce is a pure SaaS model with no infrastructure investment disclosed.
demand_pricing: Snapdeal fashion NMV up 31% YoY in H1; active fashion listings up 91% YoY to about 95 lakh; active sellers doubled YoY.
Repeat volumes about 80% of Snapdeal volumes; top 10% customers buy 17 times a year vs 13 times in FY24; payback on new customers 12 to 18 months.
Festive season shifted from Q2 last year to mainly Q3 this year, which dampened Q2 NMV growth; October first 15 days delivered unit growth of 60% YoY.
Snapdeal targets INR300 to INR800 value segment; Gen Z made up nearly two-thirds of new customers in H1; 80% of sales from outside metros.
Unicommerce serves 8,500+ clients across Uniware, Shipway and ConvertWay, including Fabindia, Hidesign, Lenskart and Mamaearth, with presence in six countries outside India.

qa_highlights.question: How are CAC and cohort payback evolving for new app customers, and what are repeat purchase economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Achint Setia said repeat volumes are about 80%+ of Snapdeal volumes, repeat frequency rose 11% YoY in H1, and CAC is healthy with payback typically 12 to 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Which AI initiatives show measurable outcomes versus early-stage investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited conversational search at 1 crore+ monthly intent-driven searches, Snap&Shop image search at 4 crore+ monthly discovery views, 81%+ of orders influenced by AI discovery, 89% of support queries resolved by SIA AI, and 90% cut in seller onboarding time.

qa_highlights.question: Is Snapdeal shifting strategy to focus mainly on fashion, with BPC and home taking a backseat?
qa_highlights.answer: Achint Setia said fashion share rose from 57% in H1 FY26 to 68%+ in H1 FY27, the three core categories (fashion, home, beauty and personal care) should keep a similar mix, and the overall business should keep growing in the 30s.

qa_highlights.question: What was the quantified impact of the festive shift to Q3 on overall growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify and said Q2 and Q3 should be viewed together once Q3 results are out; early indicators show 60% YoY volume growth in the first 15 days of October.

risks_watch: Adjusted EBITDA loss widened YoY to INR8.6 crore in Q2 FY27 from INR2.2 crore; H2 profitability recovery depends on lower Unicommerce investment and festive leverage.
Snapdeal overall NMV growth (10%) lagged delivered units (16%), implying lower average order value; monitor NMV growth in Q3 FY27.
Unicommerce growth guidance of 15%+ (Uniware) and 20%+ (Shipway) starts only from Q4 FY27; H1 growth was 15%.
Festive timing shift makes Q2 and Q3 comparisons noisy; management has not quantified the impact.

Snapdeal's proposition rests on unbranded value fashion, and management acknowledged that a consumer trust gap needs AI-led fit and discovery tools; no data on rural penetration or repeat trends by region was given.
544962|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on AI initiatives, fashion growth and the October start, but cautious on near-term profitability, with the festive shift used to explain moderated H1 growth. Management avoided quantifying the festive impact and deferred to Q3 results.
key_quotes: Our focus on profitability is visible sequentially.
We also expect the pace of incremental investments to moderate in the second half of the year, ensuring that we demonstrate higher profitability and stronger operating leverage in H2 FY27.
Our top customers buy 17 times a year, and that has also grown from 13 times a year a couple of years ago.
We expect the portfolio of this category share to be largely in the same ballpark as it is today, and the overall business we expect to continue grow in 30s as we move forward.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to INR8.6 crore from about INR18.3 crore in Q1, and management targets higher Unicommerce profitability and operating leverage in H2 FY27 as incremental investment moderates, though festive spend weighed on Q2.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects Snapdeal to keep growing in the 30s%, delivered units rose 16% in H1 with October first-15-day units up 60% YoY, and active fashion listings grew 91% to about 95 lakh.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Model is asset-light and zero-inventory with no capex or capacity figures given, and Unicommerce is pure SaaS with no infrastructure investment disclosed, so no capex trigger is evident.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Snapdeal guides to 30s% growth and Unicommerce to 15%+ Uniware and 20%+ Shipway from Q4 FY27, while H1 Unicommerce growth was only 15% and Snapdeal overall NMV grew 10%, so an upgrade depends on festive-shift catch-up in Q3.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Snapdeal overall NMV grew only 10% in H1 versus 16% delivered-unit growth, implying lower AOV, and the festive shift to Q3 makes Q2/Q3 comparisons noisy with no quantified impact given.

rows.label: Unicommerce profitability recovery in H2 FY27
rows.why: Management guides moderating incremental investment and stronger operating leverage at Unicommerce in H2 FY27, after three quarters of stepped-up spend that moderated adjusted EBITDA; H1 revenue grew 15% to INR110.4 crore.

rows.label: Snapdeal fashion momentum into festive Q3
rows.why: Fashion NMV grew 31% in H1, fashion share rose to about 68% from 57%, and October first-15-day delivered units grew 60% YoY, with festive volume shifting into Q3.

rows.label: Snapdeal AOV and NMV conversion
rows.why: Overall NMV grew 10% against 16% delivered-unit growth, so average order value is lagging and needs to recover to convert volume into NMV growth.

tone.note: Management was confident on AI initiatives, fashion growth and the October start, and cautious on near-term profitability; analysts pressed on CAC and payback, and on the festive-shift impact, which management declined to quantify and deferred to Q3 results.

544995|2026-09.headline: Fusion CX Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.1% YoY to INR 5,253 mn, PAT up 31.3% to INR 586 mn, while EBITDA margin fell 110 bps to 18.6% on training costs.
544995|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 5,253 mn (+22.1% YoY, +7.1% QoQ), with 16.8 pp organic and 5.2 pp inorganic (VAP, Australia) contribution. Reported EBITDA was INR 976 mn (+15.2%) at an 18.6% margin, down 110 bps YoY, which management attributes to training costs for two top-five clients ahead of a Q3 ramp-up; management says margin would have been about 20% without it. PAT was INR 586 mn (+31.3%), helped mainly by lower finance cost after the October 2026 listing. H1 FY27 revenue was INR 10,158 mn (+20.4%), with EBITDA of INR 1,927 mn and PAT of INR 1,142 mn.

segments.name: Revenue by geography
segments.commentary: US and Canada 81%, India 9.9%, Europe 4.3%, Australia and others about 4.8% of revenue (as stated on the call).

segments.name: Revenue by delivery model
segments.commentary: Nearshore (Latin America, Eastern Europe, Northern Africa) 39.7%, onshore (US, Canada, Germany) 33.3%, offshore (India, Philippines) about 27%.

segments.name: Core CX verticals
segments.commentary: Telecom and utility 39.2%, BFSI 18.2%, high-tech and travel 16.1%, healthcare 14.5%, others 12% of revenue.

segments.name: AI data infrastructure (Annotera, Roborax)
segments.commentary: About 5% of Q2 revenue, with 18 clients; management targets double-digit share over time. Growing much faster than the core CX business per management; three pilots with top-tier clients in last two months.

guidance_outlook: No specific revenue guidance given; management says it aims to maintain and accelerate growth in revenue, EBITDA and PAT.
Q3 FY27 expected to be seasonally stronger than H1, led by healthcare, retail and some telecom, with higher US healthcare enrolment activity and festive promotions.

Margin to recover as training costs roll off: two top-five clients ramp up in Q3, with training billable only after 5-8 weeks of training and production go-live. Management expects EBITDA margin to return to prior levels by end FY27 (some improvement, not a specific number).
Employee cost expected to stay within the current 65%-68% of revenue range, plus or minus 1%.
Australia/NZ expansion (VAP, Philippines delivery) expected to show results in 6-12 months, with possible India delivery added for time-zone fit.
impacx integration over six to eight months; VAP integration over the next few months.
Interim dividend of INR 0.75 per share (75% of face value INR 1) declared on 13 November 2026 for FY26; record date to be announced. First dividend as a listed company.
capex_capacity: Company has about 15,000 people, 42 delivery locations across 14 countries, and serves about 750 customers.
Around 40% of IPO proceeds deployed since listing, mainly debt reduction and the impacx acquisition; balance for platform upgrade, overseas debt repayment, general corporate purpose and acquisitions.
About INR 60 crore raised in the IPO to augment AI data infrastructure investment over two years; about INR 70 crore invested in the Omind AI platform over six years.
AI Data Forge platform for the AI data infrastructure business to be launched within 30 days of the call.

Acquisitions: VAP (Melbourne HQ, delivery from Philippines) completed August 2026; impacx (Western Germany, about EUR 12 mn revenue, about 250 employees, onshore Germany and nearshore Greece) completed about 2-3 days before the call. Both acquired at about 4-4.5x EBITDA.
demand_pricing: Organic growth 16.8% YoY in Q2 and 12.7% in H1; management says these rates are well above the industry average and expects the trend to continue.
Overall growth FY24-FY26 at a CAGR of about 35% including acquisitions.
Top 1 client about 20% of revenue (down from earlier); top 5 at 36.5%, top 10 at 48.9%. Top 5 clients have an average tenure of 13 years, top 10 11.5 years, top 20 10.3 years.
Voice about 70% and non-voice about 30% of Q2 revenue.
Demand for nearshore and onshore contact centres accelerating; strongest traction in the health plan business, with AI data, telecom and BFSI also growing.
Australia targeted at BFSI (mortgage broking, financial planning), plus auto and retail; management cites manpower shortages and better pay there.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins expand in H2 as training costs for top-client ramp-ups roll off?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Training runs 5-8 weeks including certification and is billed only once clients go into production, so benefits show in Q3 with higher production revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter Australia, and is there an opportunity for Indian players?
qa_highlights.answer: Australia and New Zealand face manpower shortages and pay well. The initial focus is BFSI, with auto and retail next; management also plans to add India as a delivery location for time-zone fit, with results expected in 6-12 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the TCV/ACV and traction in AI data infrastructure?
qa_highlights.answer: No TCV or ACV disclosed. The company has 18 clients in the segment, three top-tier clients in pilots over the last two months, and a pipeline described as very strong without quantification.

qa_highlights.question: What valuation were the acquisitions done at, and is more M&A planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Both FY27 acquisitions were at about 4-4.5x EBITDA. Management says M&A is an ongoing growth lever but gave no specific guidance on further deals.

qa_highlights.question: Why is organic growth lower than the 35% cited, and what is the voice/non-voice and AI mix?
qa_highlights.answer: The 35% is total growth including acquisitions; organic growth was 16.8% in Q2 and 12.7% in H1. Voice is about 70% and AI/DI about 5% of Q2 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth reach about 25% YoY over the next two years, and will margins return to earlier levels by FY27-end?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical growth guidance; management is chasing growth. It expects margins to recover by end FY27 as training costs fall away.

risks_watch: Q2 margin dip from training costs for two top-five clients; Q3 ramp-up must convert into billable production revenue as planned.
Growth is heavily weighted to the US and Canada (81%) and to telecom and utility (39.2%), with top 5 clients at 36.5% of revenue.
AI data infrastructure is about 5% of revenue and needs to scale to the double-digit share management targets; no TCV, ACV or pipeline figures disclosed.
Integration of VAP and impacx, and the earn-out-style consideration tied to impacx performance; watch the Australia and Germany ramp.
Organic growth decelerated from about 35% FY24-26 CAGR (total growth) to 12.7% in H1 FY27; watch whether the organic rate holds.
544995|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term growth, AI differentiation and M&A, but cautious on specifics: management declined to give revenue or margin guidance and gave no AI deal values. Tone is notably open on Q3 seasonality and margin recovery timing.
key_quotes: As of now, we are not providing any specific guidance, but as I mentioned in my conclusion, from a go-forward perspective we are chasing growth
Had this expenditure not been incurred, our EBITDA would have been around 20% approx.
Pipeline continues to be very strong.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell 110 bps YoY to 18.6% on training costs; management says it would have been about 20% without them, and two top-five clients ramp in Q3 with margin expected to return to prior levels by end FY27 (qualitative, no number).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two top-five client ramp-ups in Q3 and acquired capacity from VAP (Aug 2026) and impacx (about 250 employees, about EUR 12 mn revenue) being integrated over 6-8 months, though no new plants or seats are quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Organic growth was 16.8% in Q2 and 12.7% in H1, management expects the trend to continue, and Q3 is seasonally stronger with healthcare enrolment and festive promotions.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure disclosed and no new plant planned; ~INR 60 crore IPO money is earmarked for AI data infrastructure over two years and ~INR 70 crore for the Omind platform over six years, so further capex is plausible but not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric revenue or margin guidance, so there is no baseline to raise; it only said it aims to maintain and accelerate growth.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 ramp-up must convert into billable production revenue, and training costs for top-five clients drove the Q2 margin dip to 18.6%; any slip in the ramp would push margin recovery out.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AI Data Forge platform for the AI data infrastructure business is set to launch within 30 days of the call; the segment is about 5% of Q2 revenue across 18 clients and management targets a double-digit share over time.

rows.label: Australia/NZ expansion (VAP, Philippines delivery)
rows.why: Management expects results in 6-12 months, targeting BFSI, auto and retail where manpower shortages and better pay are cited, with possible India delivery added.

rows.label: AI data infrastructure pilots converting
rows.why: Three pilots with top-tier clients started in the last two months on a base of 5% of Q2 revenue, but no TCV, ACV or pipeline value was disclosed.

rows.label: Interim dividend INR 0.75/share
rows.why: Declared 13 Nov 2026 for FY26 at 75% of face value INR 1, the first dividend as a listed company; record date still to be announced.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term growth, AI differentiation and M&A and open on Q3 seasonality and margin recovery, but declined numeric guidance and AI deal values; analysts pressed on organic growth versus the 35% headline CAGR and on AI mix.

544997|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 37.2% to ₹144.98 crore and PAT grew 171% to ₹8.4 crore, with EBITDA margin at 25.7%.
544997|2026-09.overview: Shree Vasu Logistics reported strong H1 FY27 (half year ended 30 September 2026) standalone results, with revenue from operations up 37.2% YoY and EBITDA up 38.6%. Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹80.2 crore grew 43.2% YoY and 23.9% QoQ, while Q2 EBITDA margin eased to 25.6% from 25.8% in Q1. Management attributed growth to new client wins, repeat business in new territories, and added leadership in execution. The call was brief, and Q&A was mostly from individual participants on client concentration, M&A, fleet and EV plans, and insurance.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹13.6 crore YoY; margin 25.6% vs 25.8% in Q1
vs ₹1.2 crore YoY; vs ₹3.3 crore in Q1

segments.name: Third-party logistics (3PL)
segments.commentary: Covers CNF and depot operations, in-plant logistics, secondary transportation, and e-commerce and quick-commerce infrastructure. No segment-wise revenue split was given on the call.

segments.name: Secondary transportation (PTL)
segments.commentary: Combines own fleet with partner vehicles. Management said about 125 owned vehicles are used, with market-hired and contract transporters and couriers for smaller loads. No segment-wise revenue split was given.

segments.name: Warehouse leasing
segments.commentary: Described as steady annuity-style income. The company has 2.6 million sq ft of warehousing space. No segment-wise revenue split was given.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance was given for FY27 revenue, margin, or capex.
Management expects client base to keep broadening, with new clients added continuously alongside repeat business from clients in new territories.
Company plans to scale up in all zones over the coming months, with regional team setups in place across India.
Strategy: expand warehousing in high-demand zones, adopt supply chain automation, and deepen relationships with marquee enterprise clients.
EV fleet adoption is slow for now because acquisition and running costs are above normal vehicles; the company may shift when costs are back-to-back covered by clients.
capex_capacity: Footprint: operations in 16 states and 1 union territory across 43 cities, with 2.6 million sq ft of warehousing space.

Fleet: 100-plus owned vehicles per the prepared remarks; a participant cited 750 vehicles, and the answer put owned fleet at about 125 and said other modes are market-hired, contract transporters and couriers. The two fleet figures were not reconciled on the call.
Plan to scale up warehousing footprints in high-demand zones; no capex amount or commissioning timeline was disclosed.
Over 10,000 trained employees and a proprietary technology stack that supports zero-phone-call operations.
demand_pricing: Client base: about 136 enterprise clients; around 30% of business comes from the top 20 clients.
Named clients include Dabur, Parle, and JK Tyres, which are served across multiple locations.
Management said growth came from a strong order book from new clients and repeat business from existing clients in new territories.
Management said it was able to turn around new business started in the prior year.
Pricing and realisation commentary was not discussed on the call.

qa_highlights.question: How concentrated is the client book, and what is the renewal and churn experience with legacy clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 136 clients, with about 30% of business from the top 20. Management said the company is not dependent on one or two clients and that the business is long-term and does not rely on renewal activity, since it holds large stock for clients.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company evaluating acquisitions, and how does it weigh inorganic growth against greenfield capacity given leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is open to acquisition offers but is focused on organic growth for now. Leverage was not discussed.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the fleet is owned versus attached or hired, what is utilisation, and what is the EV plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 125 vehicles are owned and the rest are market-hired on a day-to-day basis, with contract transporters and couriers for small loads. EVs have been deployed, but cost is higher, so the company is going slow and will decide on a comparative cost basis. Utilisation was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What are the insurance coverage and claim experience for vehicles, and is there any GST exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one or two accident incidents occur in a year across India. Clients' invoices cover the goods, and the client's survey insurer handles claims. Management said there is no GST demand on this.

risks_watch: Client concentration: about 30% of revenue from the top 20 clients, and no client-level detail was disclosed.
Fleet dependence on market-hired vehicles, which may be exposed to availability and cost pressure.
EV transition costs remain above conventional vehicles, which may delay fleet modernisation.
Q2 EBITDA margin dipped QoQ to 25.6% from 25.8% even as revenue rose 23.9%.
Leverage and capex funding were not discussed, even though an investor asked about them.
Participant-cited fleet size of 750 vehicles versus about 125 owned plus hired capacity was not clarified.
544997|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the numbers and growth momentum, but brief and thin on detail. Management was direct on client concentration and EV timing, but gave few specifics on capex, leverage, or fleet size.
key_quotes: So, things that drove this performance was our strong order book for new clients, and at the same time, we strengthened our execution part by adding strong leaders in our company.
So, technically speaking, we are not dependent on any, one or two clients.
So, we are open to acquisition offers, but as of now, a lot of organic growth is coming in for us, so we are focusing on that.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin eased to 25.6% from 25.8% in Q1 even as revenue rose 23.9% QoQ, and H1 margin of 25.7% is up from 24.6% in H1 FY26, so direction is mixed with no cost or pricing commentary given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management plans to scale warehousing in high-demand zones and scale up in all zones over coming months, but no quantity, capex amount or commissioning date was disclosed, and 2.6 million sq ft is the only current base.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue grew 43.2% YoY to ₹80.2 crore and 23.9% QoQ, backed by a strong new-client order book and repeat business in new territories, with client base about 136 and expanding continuously.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Warehousing scale-up is planned in high-demand zones, but utilisation was not quantified and no capex amount or board approval was disclosed, so a formal capex announcement is uncertain.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical FY27 guidance was given for revenue, margin or capex, so no upgrade can be read from the call.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Around 30% of business comes from the top 20 clients, fleet relies on market-hired vehicles exposed to cost pressure, and the Q2 margin dipped QoQ to 25.6% from 25.8%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or service launch was discussed; EV fleet adoption is slow because running costs are above conventional vehicles.

rows.label: Scale-up across all zones with regional teams
rows.why: Management said it plans to scale up in all zones over the coming months, with regional team setups already in place across India and operations in 16 states and 1 UT across 43 cities.

rows.label: Acquisition offers under consideration
rows.why: Management said it is open to acquisition offers but is focused on organic growth for now, and leverage was not discussed.

rows.label: EV fleet transition on cost basis
rows.why: EV acquisition and running costs are above normal vehicles, so management is going slow and will shift only once clients cover costs back-to-back.

tone.note: Management was confident on the growth momentum (Q2 revenue +43.2% YoY) and client breadth, but cautious and thin on capex, leverage, fleet size and EV timing; analysts probed client concentration, acquisitions, fleet ownership and insurance.

544999|2026-09.headline: Tonbo Imaging H1 FY27 revenue INR219 crore, with Q2 at INR183 crore driving the half; management guides H2 "materially better" but no numeric guidance.
544999|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR219 crore versus INR77 crore in H1 FY26, with Q2 at INR183 crore against Q1 at INR36 crore. Gross margin was INR75 crore (34.62%), below FY26's 51%, which management attributed to product mix. EBITDA was INR31.15 crore (14.2% margin) for H1 and INR44 crore (24.11%) for Q2, with employee cost largely fixed across quarters. Management stressed that performance should be judged annually, not by quarter or half, given that FY26 was 78% H2-weighted.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR77 crore in H1 FY26
vs INR40 crore in H1 FY26; FY26 gross margin 51%
vs INR11.75 crore in H1 FY26
Management referred to this as H2; context indicates H1
One bank raised cash credit from INR30 crore to INR50 crore post quarter-end

segments.name: Tactical systems
segments.commentary: Thermal weapon sights, binoculars and similar soldier-carried products; management says these are 70-80% of business. Domestic gross margin is about 40-45%. About INR250 crore of the INR408 crore contracts under negotiation are tactical.

segments.name: Platform systems
segments.commentary: Gimbals, fire control systems, weapon stations and seekers; domestic gross margin about 45-50%. Order book of INR250 crore is said to be about INR200 crore platform in an analyst's framing, which management confirmed includes both legacy and newer products. About INR150 crore of contracts under negotiation are platform.

segments.name: Directed energy (HPM)
segments.commentary: Still in development at TRL 4. Five Indian Navy and six European LOIs (11 units total). Expected first delivery 2029-30; first system cost about INR160 crore, funded by EXIM loan (INR120 crore sanctioned), iDEX ADITI grant (INR25 crore) and internal accruals (INR15 crore).

guidance_outlook: No revenue or margin guidance given; company cites recent IPO as a constraint.
Management expects H2 FY27 revenue to be materially higher than H1, and EBITDA margin to exceed H1's 14.2% on higher revenue and export mix.
Order book INR250 crore plus contracts under negotiation INR408 crore; management expects contracts under negotiation to convert by December, allowing revenue in FY27.
Management indicated INR100-200 crore of execution this year from OCPP and related orders, with the excess rolling into FY28.
R&D spend in H2 expected at about INR30 crore total, of which about INR25 crore capitalised (excluding HPM); H1 R&D about INR16 crore with INR3 crore expensed.
capex_capacity: Company is fabless and manufactures through certified partners, so capex is directed to design and IP rather than plants.
HPM directed energy first system: project cost about INR160 crore (hard cost ~INR120 crore; soft cost including ~INR20 crore capitalised employee cost over 2.5 years).
Tactical sub-assemblies held in inventory allow tactical orders to convert to revenue in three to four months if placed by December.
Platform deliveries take 6-18 months from order; tactical deliveries 3-6 months generally.
Bank cash credit being increased with the other two banks following the INR50 crore increase from one bank.
demand_pricing: Export loitering munition programme: first production order from a European state-owned company for multi-sensor stabilised seeker; option for up to EUR13 million after acceptance of FOPM units. Management said this option is included in the INR408 crore contracts under negotiation, not the INR250 crore order book.

India tactical opportunity: about 80,000 thermal weapon sights and handheld thermal imagers and about 27,000 image intensifiers in stated requirement; management expects 75,000 thermal sights, 5,000 thermal imagers, and 27,000 image intensifiers in the near-term tactical slide. International near-term opportunity about 10,000 thermal sights and monoculars.
Management claims about 65% share of the ~30,000 Indian thermal weapon sights deployed (20,000 from Tonbo) and expects to hold roughly 50% in future programmes.
Two-thirds of Q2 export-related commentary: an analyst noted INR51.5 crore Q2 revenue from the US; management confirmed these are platform subsystems but declined to name customers.
Competitors in India named as Bharat Electronics, Tata and Alpha Design; BEL Optronic Devices cited as not competing on the Arjun RCWS EO system.

qa_highlights.question: How do directed energy TAM figures reconcile (USD290 million by 2030 vs INR28,000 crore across 140 systems)?

Dividends were not committed; management said growth is the priority and the first year as a listed company will be used to learn before deciding on payouts.
International: management targets 10 to 15 sizeable partners (not niche markets), using a managed-service, asset-light model rather than hardware or SaaS sales; no timing given.
Management said the Gemini offer's initial term is 18 months and it has not yet reached 12 months; no decision yet on charging after expiry.
Tariff increases: management said no decision yet and ARPU is not the only lever; timing will depend on market and macro conditions.
capex_capacity: 5G standalone investment is complete; management said capex for the next four to five years will not exceed FY27-level spend.
UBR (unlicensed broadband radio) home broadband stack has gone through four generations in about three years; management estimates a lead of at least 2.5 to 3 years over the nearest competitor.
Unlicensed UBR cost per user is about $3 against ARPU of about $6, per management, supporting the high-to-low ARPU market strategy.
Management said no incremental spectrum or capex is needed to convert the 4G base to 5G, per the call.
Radisys (already owned) is the existing channel for technology supply to operators, cited as the model for partnerships without direct competition.
demand_pricing: Management sees 340 million new mobility users (240 million from 2G users with other operators, ~100 million from demographic additions over five years).
Fixed broadband penetration is ~20% of ~330 million homes (~64 million connected); management targets ~46% by FY2031 and sees 150 million as a potential fixed broadband opportunity.
Digital economy target of $1.4 trillion cited; 80 million small merchants and 350,000 leased lines are cited as enterprise opportunities.
Digital services: Gemini voice AI usage rose from 2 minutes to over 7 minutes; home subscribers pay about 15% more for 13 OTT apps bundled, per management.
Competition: management said Jio's FWA base is 2x the nearest operator and it expects 5G adds to be driven by 4G-to-5G migration and share gains from other operators.

qa_highlights.question: Go-to-market for digital services, scale expected over 2-3 years, and international partnership timing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said digital revenue will come from enterprise, home and mobility; partnership talks are two-way, with equal engagement on UBR and full OSS/BSS stack; no timing was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why there is no converged single bill for connectivity and digital services.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is focusing on converged go-to-market and one bill, but said that story is still to play out.

qa_highlights.question: Free cash flow, dividends and capex intensity given the asset-light model.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said capex has peaked and will not exceed last year's level for four to five years; management said growth is the priority and dividends will be considered after the first listed year.

qa_highlights.question: Tariff hikes and ARPU, given about 2.5 years since last hike.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tariffs depend on several factors and it will decide at the right time; ARPU rose 3.5% YoY organically, and the focus is digital services realisations.

qa_highlights.question: Conflict of interest in international partnerships, given Jio's own connectivity business.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not give technology to domestic players, will avoid competing with partners, and the Radisys model is the reference for partnerships.

qa_highlights.question: AI monetisation (token charges) and Gemini pricing after free period.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Gemini deal runs 18 months, is not near expiry, and that AI will be offered via the telecom harness to the full base; no token charging decided.

qa_highlights.question: Starlink and satellite competition in India and the US.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said satellite direct-to-device capacity is far lower than terrestrial (about 20 kbps per sq km), that Jio covers 99% of India's homes, and that it plans its own LEO system as a complement.

qa_highlights.question: Financial metrics that management wants to hit over five to seven years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a single number and said it will track market share, deployment, and ARPU uplift; it cited FY26 EBITDA above $8 billion.

risks_watch: ARPU growth relies mainly on mix (+3.5% YoY); no tariff action has been taken in about 2.5 years, and timing is undecided.
Digital services revenue is still small (standalone revenue ₹4,881 Cr); the monetisation case depends on partner (3P) adoption and Gemini economics after the 18-month free term.
International strategy has zero customers and zero revenue; partnerships are not yet signed and no timing was given.
Competition from satellite (Starlink) and other FWA players; management claims a 2.5 to 3 year technology lead, which is not independently verified.
Watch next quarter for: any tariff move, first international partner announcement, converged billing rollout, and dividend policy.
545004|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, operating leverage and the IPO; management was firm on 'growth over dividends' and did not commit to tariff timing or international partners, deferring those answers repeatedly.
key_quotes: Growth is definitely life. There is no thinking any which way, otherwise, on dividends, Reliance has always led the way and we will be trying to follow the same things.
We do not want to be dependent on it, at the right time, those can happen.

We want to think maybe 10 to 15 partners that give us sheer scale and again, what I want to highlight to everyone is like you will think this is only for the developing markets, it is not, it is for the developed markets also.
Dan Bailey: the critical thing here is that every one of these telcos is facing the same issues that we have already faced, and we are going there to solve their issues.

rows.why: Tariff action is undecided after about 2.5 years without a hike, and ARPU growth of 3.5% relies mainly on mix, so ARPU delivery is not locked in.

rows.why: Digital services are growing (standalone revenue up 23% YoY to ₹4,881 Cr) and Gemini voice AI usage rose from 2 to over 7 minutes, but no specific launch dates were given.

rows.label: International partnerships (10-15 partners, asset-light)
rows.why: Management targets 10 to 15 sizeable partners with zero customers and zero revenue today, and no partner has been signed or timed.

rows.why: Management said growth is the priority and the first listed year is for learning, so no payout is committed in the window.

545005|2026-09.headline: Paras Healthcare Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23% to INR 511 crore and operating EBITDA 47% to INR 120 crore, margin 23.5%.
545005|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's first earnings call after its listing on 28 October 2026. Revenue from operations grew 23% YoY to INR 511 crore, operating EBITDA rose 47% to INR 120 crore, and PAT reached INR 40.3 crore versus INR 12.4 crore a year earlier. Growth came from the mature cluster (revenue up 8.5%), emerging hospitals (up 27%) and new hospitals Srinagar and Kanpur (revenue up 2.4x), which turned EBITDA-positive in Q2. Working capital absorbed INR 172 crore in H1, lifting receivables to INR 518 crore and DSO to about 92 days, while Udaipur was softer due to a suspended Rajasthan state government scheme.

segments.name: Mature hospitals (Gurgaon, Patna, Panchkula, Darbhanga)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue up 8.5% and H1 revenue up 9.1%; Q2 operating EBITDA margin 29.6% (+360 bps), H1 28.9%; H1 occupancy 76.5%.

segments.name: Emerging hospitals (Ranchi, Udaipur)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue up 27.2%, H1 up 43.2%; H1 EBITDA margin 18.3% vs 12.4%; H1 occupancy 68.6% vs 49.1%. Ranchi delivered 25.8% EBITDA margin in Q2; Udaipur was softer.

segments.name: New hospitals (Srinagar, Kanpur)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 139% in Q2 and 147% in H1; operating EBITDA turned from negative INR 13 crore in FY26 to INR 15.8 crore in Q2 and above INR 25 crore in H1; H1 margin 18.7%; H1 occupancy 68.4% vs 27.8%.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or earnings guidance given; management pointed to cohort trends for modelling.
Long-term steady-state blended EBITDA margin envisaged in the mid-20s percent; management explicitly said this is not guidance.
About 200-250 beds to be operationalised in Kanpur (remaining half of 435-bed capacity) and Ranchi, taking operational beds from about 1,500 to about 1,800, by end of FY27.
Emerging hospitals expected to move to mature cohort over 4-7 years, then reach low-to-mid 20s margins before mid-to-high 20s when mature.
Gurgaon Golf Course Extension (300 beds) and Ludhiana (500 beds, next year) are the next capacity additions; 800 beds coming on stream over the next 12-18 months to 20-24 months.
Remaining INR 125 crore of IPO proceeds to be used for debt repayment, lowering interest cost.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about INR 90 crore across units, including payments for Gurgaon 2 (Golf Course Extension).
Kanpur has 435 bed capacity; roughly half opened, two wings yet to open by end of FY27.
Ludhiana 500-bed expansion expected next year; Gurgaon 2 adds 300 beds.
New and upcoming facilities are to remain asset-light; M&A, greenfield, brownfield and O&M models are open but current focus is on the two projects.
Quaternary programmes: liver transplant (Gurgaon, extended to Panchkula and Patna), kidney and bone marrow transplant; robotic surgery in Gurgaon, Patna, Panchkula, Ranchi and Udaipur (ortho).
demand_pricing: Group occupancy Q2 FY27 76.3% vs 62.5% YoY; H1 73% vs 59%; occupied bed days up 23.9% to 201,000.
Inpatient volumes up 27.3% and outpatient volumes up 20.4% in H1 YoY.
ARPOB H1 FY27 INR 48,900 vs INR 48,400; ALOS 2.8 days vs 2.9 days.
H1 payor mix: 32% cash/self-pay, 24% insurance, 44% government schemes and PSUs.

Rajasthan state government scheme temporarily suspended across multiple Rajasthan hospitals, hurting Udaipur; management says Udaipur cash and insurance business grew in absolute terms and recovered 30-40% of lost state scheme business.
Kanpur EBITDA margin improved from -22.8% to 15.6%; Kanpur occupancy 78.4% in H1 FY27 vs 22.7% in H1 FY26. Srinagar occupancy 60.4% in H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Udaipur soft this quarter and could its revenue fall YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet Aggarwal said the Rajasthan state government scheme was under review and temporarily suspended across multiple hospitals; Udaipur's cash and insurance business grew, recovering 30-40% of lost state-scheme business. Management is working to reduce government-scheme dependence.

qa_highlights.question: Why is receivables build-up (cash flow negative INR 172 crore working capital) so large year-on-year?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Bidani attributed it to 25% business growth, a higher share of empanelments in new hospitals, and lumpy payments from certain payor groups; DSO rose from about 79 days (March) to 92 days (September). Trade receivables rose from INR 87.5 crore to INR 124 crore YoY per the analyst; management said it expects it to settle as payor mix improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 50 crore item in other financial assets in operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Bidani said it is a long-term fixed deposit with regular bankers, created from the INR 80 crore equity infusion in April 2025 and classified as non-current under accounting standards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin for mature hospitals and how will margins evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Bidani said new hospitals move from negative to mid-to-high teens margins, then emerging, then mature (currently mid-to-high 20s blended). Long-term steady-state blended margin envisaged in the mid-20s; not a guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is there ALOS and seasonality sustainability into Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet Aggarwal said ALOS has consistently been 2.8-3.0 days and expected to continue; case mix, daycare and robotic surgery drive it. Seasonality reflects North and East India locations; occupancy to be supported by existing capacity and bed additions.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company stay asset-light and is acquisition a low priority?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Nagar said Gurgaon and Ludhiana remain asset-light; M&A, greenfield, brownfield and PPP are open, but current focus is delivering the two projects over the next two years.

risks_watch: Receivables rose from INR 350 crore (March 2026) to INR 518 crore (September 2026) and DSO to about 92 days; H1 OCF only INR 68 crore against PAT of INR 90 crore.
Rajasthan state scheme suspension affecting Udaipur; revenue may decline YoY there until scheme resumes.
Dependence on government and PSU schemes at 44% of H1 payor mix.
Ramp-up of Kanpur (about half of 435 beds still unopened) and Ranchi beds by year-end; Srinagar occupancy at 60.4%.
Execution of Gurgaon Golf Course Extension and Ludhiana (800 beds) and doctor recruitment for specialty and quaternary programmes; talent shortage cited in Darbhanga.
No formal guidance; watch next quarter's disclosures on DSO, net debt and interest cost savings.
545005|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, with candour on weak spots: management openly flagged Udaipur's softness and working-capital build-up, but gave no numeric guidance, deferring to a long-term margin model framed as not guidance.
key_quotes: Margin expanded by 390 basis points to 23.5%.
Of the INR 500 crores of fresh issue, INR 375 crores has already gone to repay and prepay borrowings.
Udaipur was softer, and of course, the teams will talk about it, our operations will talk about it.
There is no guidance as such which we are sharing.

vs INR 12.4 crore YoY; EPS INR 4

rows.why: Receivables rose from INR 350 crore (March 2026) to INR 518 crore (September) and DSO to about 92 days from about 79 days; management expects it to settle as payor mix improves, but no timeline or number was given.

rows.why: Srinagar and Kanpur turned from negative INR 13 crore EBITDA in FY26 to INR 15.8 crore in Q2 FY27, with H1 margin 18.7% and occupancy 68.4% vs 27.8%.

545008|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 PAT rose 35% YoY to INR169 crore; fee-paying AUM reached INR49,164 crore, up 23% on a 3-year CAGR.
545008|2026-09.overview: First earnings call after the company's recent listing, covering Q2 and H1 FY27 (period ended 30 September 2026). Total income for H1 was INR616 crore (up 35% YoY) and management and advisory fee was INR333 crore (up 24% YoY). Q2 PAT was INR88 crore (up 28% YoY, up 9% QoQ), with PAT yield stable at about 0.71-0.72% of fee-paying AUM. Management guided to 20-30% medium-term growth in fee-paying AUM and PAT, and said the Q1 figures included the full exit of Infrastructure Fund 1, which affected income and expenses.

financial_highlights.change: 23% 3-year rolling CAGR; 28% YoY from about INR38,500 crore
up from about 25% a year ago

financial_highlights.value: about INR95,000 crore (including dry powder and commitments)
INR7 per share (140% of face value)

segments.name: Fundraising
segments.commentary: Raised about INR8,250 crore across special situations, infrastructure and private equity funds in H1 FY27, plus about INR12,000 crore in listed InvIT strategies, totalling close to INR20,000 crore in H1.

segments.name: Deployment and realisations
segments.commentary: Won the TOT-19 bundle under the National Monetisation Plan at INR2,259 crore (about 600 lane km, Tamil Nadu), and acquired a 95% occupied Grade A office park in Pune of about 1 million sq ft. Collected upwards of INR6,300 crore of realisations across strategies.

segments.name: Own-and-operate assets
segments.commentary: Owns and operates about 5.6 million sq ft of completed office space, about 7,700 km of roads, 1.73 GW of solar and about 1,800 circuit km of transmission lines.

segments.name: Credit
segments.commentary: Over 17 years, invested about INR43,000 crore across 190+ companies and realised more than INR46,000 crore. Growth capital given to Cyient Semiconductors, Gujarat Themis and Great White.

guidance_outlook: Medium to long-term growth of 20-30% in fee-paying AUM and PAT.
Aspirational PAT yield of 65-70 basis points on fee-paying AUM.
Target ROE of 30%.
VAR (variable/carry) PAT expected at 25-30% of overall PAT, now spread across 7 funds and 5 strategies.
Aspiration to distribute about 40-50% of profits; long-term dividend payout of around 50% of annual earnings is under consideration, and management invited views on it.

Special Situations Fund, Infrastructure Yield Fund and second vintage of Commercial Real Estate Fund are in fundraising over the next few quarters; Private Equity Fund 2 expected to be nearly 3x Fund 1.
capex_capacity: Dry powder within AUM estimated at INR20,000-25,000 crore; finance team to provide exact figure.
Over FY26 and H1 FY27, about INR31,000 crore raised, of which about INR11,000 crore is listed InvIT capital and about INR20,000 crore is fund capital, mostly available as dry powder.
Infrastructure Fund 1 fully exited in H1 FY27 (gross IRR about 19.3%).
Recent acquisitions: TOT-19 road assets (INR2,259 crore) and the Pune office park (about 1 million sq ft).
demand_pricing: Distribution cost averages about 30 bps of AUM; with a 50:50 institutional-to-HNI mix, P&L distribution cost is about 60 bps. Amortised over 6-7 years, this is about 3.5-4% of distribution cost. Cash payment is 1/3 upfront and 2/3 over the fund's trail period.

Institutional clients (about 49% of AUM) are approached directly; HNI, UHNI and family office clients (about 51%) come through distributors. Management said there is no VAR sharing with distributors. Distributor concentration was not disclosed.
About 77% of AUM comes from repeat clients; 5,750+ unique client relationships.
Management fee grew 23% YoY versus FPAUM growth of 28%, because the Infrastructure Fund 1 exit reduced fee-paying AUM and new capital accrues over several quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How visible is VAR (variable carry) in income and yield strategies versus PE/VC, and is the book's visibility high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said visibility is fairly high: hurdle returns do not compound because annual cash flows are paid out, the strategies are non-equity correlated, and owned assets have about 20-year contracted cash flows. Slide 14 was cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the distribution mix (direct versus external distributors), and what is the overall AUM including commitments?
qa_highlights.answer: Institutions are direct and HNI/family offices go through distributors. Total AUM is about INR95,000 crore, including dry powder that will later convert to fee-paying AUM.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the deferred distribution cost amortised in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Infrastructure Fund 1 was exited ahead of its scheduled life, so the remaining forward-period distribution cost was expensed in Q1. There is no VAR sharing with distributors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the difference in yield and unit economics between real assets and credit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said real assets are lower-beta with lower gross yields, but the funds target similar unit economics, measured net of distribution costs (Slide 15). Infrastructure Fund 1 delivered a gross IRR of about 19.3%.

qa_highlights.question: How is carry realised, and when is it paid?
qa_highlights.answer: Carry is paid after client hurdle returns are met. Because many hurdles are paid annually, carry is more certain and gets realised over time across vintages (Slide 42 illustrates this).

qa_highlights.question: What is the dry powder mix and planned fund launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Special Situations, Infrastructure Yield and CRE Fund 2 are in fundraising over the next few quarters, and PE Fund 2 is expected to be about 3x Fund 1. A breakup of the INR20,000 crore raised was promised separately.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management fee growth lower than FPAUM growth, and how does AUM convert to FPAUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Fees are calculated on daily FPAUM, so new raises flow through over several quarters, and the Infrastructure Fund 1 exit reduced the base. The AUM-to-FPAUM gap reflects repaid capital and dry powder, which is about INR20,000-25,000 crore.

risks_watch: Management fee growth (23%) trails FPAUM growth (28%) in the short term; watch whether the gap narrows as new raises get deployed.
Q1 included one-off items from the Infrastructure Fund 1 exit (distribution cost expensed early), so the quarterly run-rate needs to be read with care.
VAR concentration and timing: carry depends on hurdle returns and realisations, and the VAR share target is 25-30% of PAT.
Dry powder of about INR20,000-25,000 crore must be deployed to convert into fee-paying AUM; the detailed breakup was pending.
Distributor concentration (top three or five) was not disclosed.
Dividend payout policy (around 50% long-term) is still open for shareholder views.

key_quotes: We have grown, as I said earlier, at a 23% CAGR on a 3-year rolling basis, and which is what is also the number for 30th September 2026.

We are a standalone pure-play alternative asset manager on the income and yield side, and therefore there is no conflict with any distributor in terms of distribution of these products domestically and globally.
We have decided to keep this capability in-house even though in the short term it might look costlier, but we do believe that in the long term this is a significant strategic advantage for us.

rows.why: Management fee grew only 23% against FPAUM growth of 28%, and the dry powder breakup was deferred, so fee conversion could lag the 20-30% guide if deployment slows.
